$comment: CANONICAL turn-grading vocabulary — the single source of truth for how ANY
repo grades an agentic turn. P0a of docs/plans/agentic-tooling-best-practices-alignment.md.
WHY THIS IS DATA, NOT CODE: the only real grader (matrixDriver.js) is JS and
two of its three consumers (connector, framework) are Python. Hand-porting the
grader would create exactly the parallel-list drift this file exists to stop.
So the VOCABULARY (what counts as an error, which cards are interchangeable,
the verdict ladder, the gate ladder) lives here as language-neutral data that
both runtimes read, while the grading LOGIC stays in one place per language.
CONSUMERS:
JS     tests/live/lib/matrixDriver.js  (loads this file directly)
Python connector fsr_soc_triage/verdict_vocab.py (vendored copy + parity test)
CHANGING THIS FILE changes acceptance for every repo. Bump `version` when you
do — the Python parity test compares it and fails loudly on a stale vendor.
Classifies a tool_result payload as an error. Covers the connector's
structured failures ({ok:false}, {error}, {code}), thrown-exception text,
and the 'empty/degraded' results that silently derail a hunt (no matches,
module/connector unavailable, unknown_operation).
JS-flavoured regex source; `\b` and alternation only, so Python's `re`
compiles it unchanged. Keep it portable — no lookbehind, no named groups.
errorPattern.source: \b(error|unavailable|not available|unknown_operation|no matches|no operations|failed|exception|traceback|denied|forbidden|timed? out|invalid endpoint|invalid credentials|not configured|no close suggestion)\b

$comment: Payload shapes that look like failures but are not. `guard_redirect` is
STEERING (hunt-floor / call-once / capability guards, AGENT_HARDENING §D);
`ok:true` with a nested 'error' string is DATA, not a tool failure —
list_configured_connectors reports each config's health, and an
unconfigured imap once red-flagged the whole call.
Card-type equivalence for the expected-card gate. The widget renders
status_card / info_card / ioc_card through the SAME normalizeInfoCard path,
and the connector normalizes an IOC-consolidation deliverable to an
info_card (variant ioc_enrichment) — so for acceptance they are ONE
deliverable. status_card is deliberately NOT folded in: it is a
connector-health deliverable, semantically distinct from an info/ioc
finding, so a scenario wanting an info deliverable must not pass on a bare
status card.
The ladder, worst first. `hardFail` marks the ones that block a soft gate.
`driveError` marks the ones that are HARNESS failures, not agent behaviour —
those block on EVERY gate including xfail (an xfail that swallowed a drive
error would report 'XPASS (promote?)' for a turn that never sent a prompt).
Per-row gating: the matrix must hold rows that must stay clean AND rows
documenting an open bug. A suite that goes perma-red on a known bug gets
ignored; one that blocks only on hard-FAIL ships DEGRADED regressions
silently. forbidRedFlags[] overrides EVERY gate — that is what keeps an
xfail honest.
errBudget: tool errors tolerated before DEGRADED. minTools: a triage that
runs 0 tools is an LLM summarizer, not an investigator.
